title: Firework Trailing Smoke
goal: Modify the scene and complete the trailing smoke: during the firework's ascent, smoke should be emitted in the opposite direction of travel. title: Firework Trailing Sparks
goal: Modify the scene and complete the trailing sparks: after sparks are emitted opposite the firework launch direction, they should fall toward the ground. Use bright yellow highlight particles close to the launch point, with fast dissipation and backward initial velocity. The sparks should have trailing streaks caused by visual persistence.

title: Firework Head Halo
goal: Modify the scene and complete the head halo: attach a bright yellow highlighted core to the rocket head to simulate a rising bright point in the night sky. Continuously and rapidly emit a small number of large particles to simulate flickering light.

title: Firework Explosion Effect
goal: Use particle systems to modify scene objects and complete the explosion effect. When the firework explodes, use a sphere to simulate the firework shape. At the instant of explosion, particle speed should be extremely high, but because of air resistance, particles should quickly decelerate in a short time, forming a visual effect of "bursting outward, instantly freezing, then beginning to fall". At the explosion center, the energy is extremely high, so it is usually pure white, like an overexposed flash. It then quickly transitions to vivid pure yellow, and finally becomes dark red before extinguishing. The residual sparks after the explosion should be affected by gravity and gently sway left and right while falling, creating a natural parabolic downward motion.
